successors.name: Republic of India
successors.text: Sikkim: the Denjong of Phuntsog Namgyal's consecration at Yuksom

ledger.x: 1642: Phuntsog Namgyal is consecrated the first Chogyal at Yuksom.

Darjeeling, Kalimpong, Limbuwan and the Terai between the Mechi and the Teesta are Sikkim's before they are lost (1835 'cession of Darjeeling', 1706 Kalimpong 'said to have come under the control of Bhutan', 1788 'took Limbuana', 1817 'territory annexed by the Nepalese' returned).

The Sikkimese Terai: the Treaty of Tumlong page says 'the Gorkhas overran the Sikkimese Terai before the 1814-16 Anglo-Nepalese War', the Titalia page that the land east of the Mechi was 'seized by the Gorkhas of Nepal'.
1861: 'the British annexed the whole of the Darjeeling district and the Terai in 1861'.
1888: 'A British military expedition expelled Tibetan forces from Sikkim.'
1888: the Tibetans expelled; the Convention of Calcutta (1890) has China recognise the British protectorate.
16 May 1975: the Kingdom of Sikkim ends in merger with India, after a referendum on the monarchy.

wars.name: Gorkha conquest of Limbuwan and western Sikkim
wars.outcome: The Gorkhas took Limbuwan and Rabdentse; the king fled to Tibet; the lost land was recovered only in part in 1817.

wars.name: British expedition to Sikkim
wars.outcome: The punitive expedition that followed the Campbell-Hooker affair of 1849 ended with the Treaty of Tumlong (March 1861) and the annexation of the Darjeeling district and the Terai.

wars.name: Tibetan incursion of 1888
wars.outcome: A British military expedition expelled Tibetan forces from Sikkim.

certainty.note: A Himalayan kingdom with no surveyed frontier; Limbuwan, the Terai, Kalimpong and Darjeeling are bridged lands.
The Mechi and Teesta rivers of the 1817 treaty and, from 1861, the Sikkim frontier as the British drew it; the Tibetan frontier was settled by the 1890 Convention of Calcutta.
